edition: NS-01 | Greatstone internal facilitator edition | v1.0 | 21 October 2026
purpose: Purpose: provoke a bigger yet owned and testable strategic ambition; convert it into an approved North Star Record, strategic hypotheses and a directed evidence plan for the GDXP™.
guardrails: This is a discovery and strategic challenge, not a sales presentation for a unified portal or AI product. Gordon owns the North Star; Greatstone tests and stretches it.
Do not confuse what Indago wants with what is already true. Mark aspirations, source statements, hypotheses and independently verified facts separately.
Explore unconstrained possibility first, then return to evidence, economics, rights, organisational capability and realistic sequencing.
No scoring questionnaire. Use live dialogue, follow-up questions, concrete examples and documented decisions.
Record Gordon’s actual words before drafting Greatstone interpretations. Obtain explicit confirmation of the final wording and record dissent or uncertainty.

baseline.proposition: IND-EV-009: technology to make delivery seamless, add client value, differentiate and reduce effort
baseline.treatment: Confirm whether still accurate; ask what success actually looks like.

baseline.proposition: IND-EV-012: ambition to become an “anything data” business / African market intelligence hub
baseline.treatment: Explore the market and competitive meaning; do not treat as approved direction.

baseline.proposition: IND-EV-018: one portal per client and digital front door
baseline.treatment: Treat as a candidate capability, not the North Star.

baseline.proposition: IND-EV-011: 10–20 institutions at roughly US$100k annually
baseline.treatment: Confirm currency, timeframe, appetite and commercial basis; currently unverified.

baseline.proposition: IND-EV-014 and 082: subscription benchmark and pooled data
baseline.treatment: Test demand, differentiation and contractual/data rights before endorsement.

baseline.proposition: IND-EV-005: automated AI calling excluded from current scope
baseline.treatment: Preserve current scope boundary; future feasibility may be explored separately.

baseline.proposition: IND-EV-116: published vision of foremost value-adding consumer insights in Africa
baseline.treatment: Ask how published vision relates to the proposed future North Star.

baselineNote: Source note: IDs are from the client-facing evidence register embedded in the project portal. All are pending Indago confirmation. These are prompts, not approved facts.

runOfShow.move: Set purpose; Gordon states current North Star without prompting
Challenge the business definition and customer outcome
Test what must remain human and what technology enables
Converge on North Star wording and 3–5 outcomes
Confirm assumptions, evidence needs and approval route

questions.heading: A. What business are we really in?
items: If Indago ceased conducting surveys tomorrow, what indispensable value would customers still pay you to deliver?  Press for the decision enabled, not the report produced.
Do customers buy research, or do they buy confidence to make better decisions? What evidence distinguishes the two?
If a new competitor offered the same research at half your price, why would your best client stay?
What would Indago stop doing if its true purpose were to improve client decisions rather than deliver projects?

questions.heading: B. A future beyond the present company
items: Imagine Indago has succeeded spectacularly in 2031. What is it famous for that it cannot do today?
Would you rather serve 20 institutions at exceptional value or 2,000 customers digitally? Why?
What would an African CEO, bank board or brand leader be able to do with Indago every Monday morning?
What would make Indago essential between research projects, rather than only when a survey is commissioned?
Which markets would you enter if geography were no longer constrained by your current operating model?

questions.heading: C. Challenge the economics and competitive advantage
items: What is the most valuable insight you generate that you currently give away within a fixed project fee?
Could revenue grow threefold without headcount growing threefold? What would have to be fundamentally different?
What must Indago uniquely own: methodology, trusted relationships, datasets, benchmarks, distribution or decision workflows?
If customers can build dashboards and generate AI summaries themselves, what remains uniquely valuable about Indago?
Would you prefer project revenue, recurring subscriptions, advisory retainers, licensing or a hybrid? What evidence would change your mind?

questions.heading: D. Challenge the client experience and product boundary
items: If a customer could configure and buy a research service without speaking to anyone, would that strengthen or weaken Indago?
Which client decisions require expert interpretation and which could safely become self-service?
Could an ongoing intelligence relationship replace periodic static reporting? What must be true for that to work?
What should a client be able to know today that they currently learn six weeks too late?

questions.heading: E. Challenge technology, AI and human advantage
items: If 80% of repetitive data processing disappeared, where should your people spend their newly available capacity?
Which parts of research must never be delegated entirely to AI because trust, methodology or judgement would suffer?
If a unified portal never existed, could you still achieve the North Star? If yes, what is truly essential?
Which AI use case would you reject even if technically possible, and why?

questions.heading: F. Challenge the courage and trade-offs
items: What is the biggest strategic bet you have avoided because the current business must keep running?
What would you deliberately NOT pursue, even if it could generate revenue?
What would you be willing to invest, change or give up to achieve this ambition?
If we recommend against the portal you originally envisaged, what evidence would make you accept that conclusion?

futures.name: A — Research excellence
futures.provocation: Indago becomes the most efficient and trusted premium research provider in its chosen markets.
futures.evidence: Process economics, quality, pricing power, renewal evidence.

futures.name: B — Continuous intelligence partner
futures.provocation: Indago provides recurring decision intelligence and measurable client outcomes.
futures.evidence: Demand, willingness to pay, delivery cadence, data rights, retention.

futures.name: C — Scalable intelligence platform
futures.provocation: Indago develops a defensible digital intelligence product and service ecosystem.
futures.evidence: Market sizing, distribution, rights, architecture, investment and adoption.

futuresAsk: Ask: Which future excites you? Which creates durable value? Which is most plausible? Could the best North Star combine elements? Do not choose an implementation architecture in this session.
sentenceAid: Use this sentence structure only as a drafting aid: “By [horizon], Indago will be [strategic identity] for [customer/market], enabling [valuable customer outcome] through [distinctive advantage], while achieving [measurable business outcomes], without compromising [principles].”
boundary: Which customers and sectors are priority?
What is the appetite for investment and risk?
What data can legally and ethically be reused?
Which activities must not be automated?
Which North Star dimensions are stretch hypotheses?
convergence: Is the statement about a business outcome, rather than an app, dashboard or AI capability?
Would customers recognise and value the proposed difference?
Does it go materially beyond today while remaining capable of staged delivery?
Is there a credible route to commercial sustainability?
Are 3–5 measurable outcomes, owners and horizons defined?
Are critical assumptions explicitly labelled for Deep Dive validation?
Has Gordon explicitly accepted the wording, or is it only a Greatstone proposal?
important: Important: An approved strategic ambition is not approval of a particular technology design, investment or implementation. Those choices depend on the subsequent Deep Dive evidence and GDXP™ recommendations.
